You think your deportation policy went too far. It was too tough.

China is denying allegations that it carried out a spy operation targeting
the CEO of computer chip giant Nvidia, Jensen Wong. Here's NPR's Jennifer Pack.
American officials have been blocking China's access to its most advanced chipsets,
yet Wong has criticized this policy. President Trump eventually let
Nvidia sell chips to China, just less advanced ones.
Now, Wong admits having an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence alleges a Chinese spy,
and says he will cooperate fully with the company's investigation into national security concerns.
NPR has not independently confirmed the affair.
China's foreign ministry calls the so-called Chinese spy narrative an attempt to smear China.
Chinese media have downplayed the spy aspect of the story. On Michael blogging platform Weibo,
the hashtag Jensen Wong admits to cheating has racked up over 580 million views.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
International climate change negotiations are kicking off in Turkey today.
The talks at the COP 31 summit began with a dire warning from international forecasters.
Here's NPR's Lauren Summer.
The way 2026 is going, it's looking like it'll be one of the hottest years on record.
That means the last 12 years are the hottest 12 years since record-keeping began,
according to a new report from the World Meteorological Organization.
Emissions from burning fossil fuels also led to a new record.
Heat-trapping gases in the atmosphere are now more than 50 percent higher than they were in 1750.
China emits the most greenhouse gases yearly, followed by the United States and India.
World leaders are negotiating their plans for reducing emissions from fossil fuels.
Most nations are not on track to meet their pledges. Lauren Summer, NPR News.
Actor and comedian Russell Brand has been sentenced in Britain
to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault.
He was convicted last week of crimes against four women between 2004 and 2009.
After hearing the victim impact statements, the judge said Brand had become a "sexual predator."
Brand denies the charges. The 51-year-old was a career chameleon who went from stand-up comic
and MTV host to a political analyst esteemed by Britain's left.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
Pope Leo's tour to Latin America has taken him to Argentina,
where he arrived yesterday greeted by a military honor guard,
as heard here through the Associated Press.
He also delivered a message that could be viewed
as a rebuke of President Xavier Millet's austerity measures.
The pontiff visited an institution that houses more than 400 people with disabilities.
The site, known as the City of Charities, has felt the severe impact of Millet's sweeping cuts
to health care and social services.
He told those he visited that their lives are a blessing, not a burden.
He later led mass, drawing an estimated two and a half million people.
Most schools across the U.S. ban cell phones in their classrooms.
NPR's Amy Held reports a growing number of teachers also
want to see laptops removed from class.
9 out of 10 U.S. public schools provide a device to every student.
Maureen Mulvaney in Minneapolis has been teaching for 23 years and says she's noticed something.
Her students have lost stamina.
They look at something that's hard and they immediately turn to AI to solve the problem.
So last year, she removed all screens from her high school AP literature class.
Real paperback.
Students read the classics and write essays by hand.
Their skills improve, she says.
What was really surprising was that the students liked it so much.
They were saying, why can't we do this in all our classes?
More are moving in that direction.
A recent Gallup poll finds nearly two-thirds of teachers say students
should spend less time on screens.
But roughly the same say some digital tools can be helpful.
Amy Held, NPR News.
